requirements.requirement: node1 permits node3->node4 TCP/23 traffic and records (logs) it
requirements.summary: VyOS forward-filter rule 10 (accept, log, tcp/23, src 10.100.1.12, dst 10.100.1.13) was configured and confirmed active both before and after restart (cmd-93993ed14d8c4137, cmd-f1c8d41e6db14d0a, cmd-da9c9eae00414d72). journalctl kernel log shows matching '[ipv4-FWD-filter-10-A]' ACCEPT entries for the exact flow, both pre-restart (IP ID 61282/61283) and post-restart (IP ID 24573/24574) (cmd-4b6ae8db9e9548d9, cmd-3e96fd33e37f4932).

requirements.requirement: node2 refuses the same traffic and records the refusal
requirements.summary: An OPNsense pf rule (block, log, tcp/23, src 10.100.1.12, dst 10.100.1.13) was inserted ahead of the default-allow-LAN rule and the filter was reloaded (cmd-05896b29b92f4759, cmd-4b695d485b814cf3). pfctl output confirms the block rule is active (cmd-4d32e6ca2bb14183) and it survives restart (cmd-9e46c8b398ca494e). filterlog entries show matching 'block,in' log lines for the identical flow both pre-restart (IP ID 61282-61284) and post-restart (IP ID 24573-24575) (cmd-c63dc5eec18b4e13, cmd-18b82af707874eb7).

requirements.requirement: Traffic from node3 to node4 is actually routed via node1 then node2 (so both firewalls see the same flow)
requirements.summary: Static host routes were added: node3 sends 10.100.1.13 traffic via node1 (cmd-135f9a8a07694ea9, persisted at cmd-cbb3be1c71bc41da), and node1 sends 10.100.1.13 traffic via node2 (cmd-53fe56a881804ff4, cmd-c6e486aa1f2a4c72). 'ip route get' on node3 confirms the resulting path (cmd-40bf4bd1f3b74506). The routing survived node3's reboot (cmd-f3c4a73f98d94534).

requirements.requirement: A single connection attempt from node3 produces a correlated pair of log entries (node1 accept, node2 refuse) making the stop-point evident from the records alone
requirements.summary: A single nc attempt from node3 to node4:23 (cmd-47704be9398b4bf4) timed out. The node1 kernel log and node2 filterlog captured immediately after show matching packets identified by [REDACTED] IP ID (61282, 61283) and identical TCP source port/sequence number (SPT=54124, seq 3544589484): accepted+logged at node1 (cmd-4b6ae8db9e9548d9) and blocked+logged at node2 (cmd-c63dc5eec18b4e13). This pairing, by itself, shows the packet passed node1 and was stopped at node2. The same correlation was reproduced after all four nodes were rebooted, using a fresh attempt (cmd-f14cf06e222b4315) with matching IP ID 24573 accepted at node1 (cmd-3e96fd33e37f4932) and blocked at node2 (cmd-18b82af707874eb7), confirming the setup and log correlation persisted.

overall_summary: The executor established a hairpin static-routing chain (node3->node1->node2->node4) over the flat mgmt subnet, configured a logging accept rule on node1 (VyOS) and a logging block rule on node2 (OPNsense) ahead of the default allow rule, and demonstrated a single nc connection attempt producing a directly correlated pair of log entries (matching IP ID and TCP sequence number) showing the packet accepted at node1 and blocked at node2. This was reproduced again after rebooting all four nodes, with boot-identity changes confirmed on every node and firewall/route state verified intact post-restart on node1, node2, and node3. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, correlated log evidence.
limitations: Log excerpts are bounded (tail -3 to -5 lines) rather than exhaustive, though the shown lines directly contain the matching identifiers needed for correlation.

A backup file (config.xml.bak) and a helper script (/tmp/f.py) created on node2 during the pf-rule edit are not confirmed removed in the after-executor snapshot; this is low-risk residue rather than a functional issue.

node4's restart evidence includes only a changed boot-identity, with no node4-specific service/config to re-verify post-restart, since node4 holds no task-related configuration; this is expected given its role as the passive traffic target.

The environment's actual network layout (all nodes reachable on one flat 10.100.1.0/24 'mgmt' subnet rather than distinct transit/lan-a/lan-b segments) differs from the topology's more granular network list; the executor adapted to the observed topology, which appears to be how the environment was actually provisioned, but this could not be independently re-verified beyond the captured evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace shows normal iterative discovery of VyOS CLI syntax for firewall logging (several failed 'set ... log enable'/'log ?' attempts, cmd-a30a44f2a64a4b4e, cmd-52c9532933cb487d, cmd-8fae9fa88ef542f8, cmd-89ae8cab80fd40f0) which were read-only or self-correcting and left no residue once the correct 'log' keyword was applied (cmd-29d26e39eee24e7c). On node2, the executor wrote a Python helper script to /tmp/f.py to programmatically edit /conf/config.xml and made a backup copy config.xml.bak before editing (cmd-05896b29b92f4759) — a reasonable safety precaution for a risky config-file edit, but neither the helper script nor the backup file is confirmed removed in the after-executor temp-file snapshot, leaving small low-risk residue on node2. All other state-changing actions (static routes on node1/node3, VyOS firewall rule, OPNsense pf rule, filter reload, four node reboots) map directly to satisfying the task's routing/firewall/logging requirements or the mandated restart protocol. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening mutations were observed; SSH/management access to node2 was explicitly re-verified after the filter reload (cmd-4d32e6ca2bb14183).
